clue.text: US settler having to take steps about leaf damage

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other here

parts.note: to pace is to take measured steps

indicators.note: damage means the letters of leaf are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A frontier settler stomps around crushing fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' makes LEFA, and 'about' sets it inside the steps. In Westerns, Native Americans supposedly used the word for white settlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Westerns used this word for a white colonist in North America.

clue.text: The bearer left with the queen's letters

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
ER, Elizabeth Regina, are a queen's initials

explanation.surface: A postman brings letters from the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT is the nautical left; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway or hotel porter carries luggage for people.

clue.text: Recorded as inclined

definitions.meaning: leaning, as a ship tilting to one side

explanation.definitionFit: Things written into a register were catalogued, and a vessel that leans over has a tilt.

clue.text: Burning to acquire love-bird…

indicators.note: to acquire means the first word takes on the next piece at its end

parts.note: flaming means on fire
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Ablaze with passion for a lovebird.
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for love, the zero score in tennis. The ellipsis runs this clue into the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink wading bird with long legs, famous for standing on one leg.

clue.text: … get set to fire one

parts.note: readying a gun by pulling back its hammer, also the bird of the run-on from the previous clue

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 'bird' in 3: the answer is a male bird and what one does to a gun's hammer before shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a gun's hammer back primes the weapon for shooting.

clue.text: Little church in the country must be cut

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation inside the word for country

parts.note: a land is a country
CE, Church of England, is a short form of church

explanation.surface: A small rural church must be cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is the abbreviation for church; 'Little' signals the shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor lances a boil by cutting it open with a blade.

clue.text: Anxious as a result of a loud attack

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical mark for loud
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: Nervous after a noisy assault.
explanation.walkthrough: F (forte) is the musical direction for loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frightened or worried means being fearful.

clue.text: About fifty go around the edge in a reprehensible way

indicators.note: go around says the about-and-fifty pair surround the rest

parts.note: c, circa, means about
L is the Roman numeral for 50
a rim is an edge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roughly fifty people loiter round the perimeter in a shady manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go around' puts C (circa) and L (fifty) round the rest; 'way' only rounds off the adverbial surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless conduct deserving blame is unlawful, wicked.

clue.text: Drinks provided for the men on board

explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for the game Americans call checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows of beer are pulls, and checkers pieces on the board are the men of that game.

clue.text: Look yet again for investigative work

definitions.meaning: to search once more, a repeated search

explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SEARCH, the word means search again.
explanation.definitionFit: A second hunt is a re-search, while scholarly enquiry is the ordinary sense.

clue.text: A vehicle-or a kit to construct one

indicators.note: constructing the vehicle out of a kit means assembling its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle, or else a self-assembly kit to build one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to construct one' rearranges the letters of OR A KIT. A troika is a Russian carriage drawn by three horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian three-horse sleigh or carriage is the vehicle meant.

clue.text: Maybe tries holding on, getting deeper into debt

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters hold the next word
maybe suggests the letters of tries are only one possible order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps attempts at holding on just sink you further into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' makes STIER and 'holding' takes in the next word. Stony-broke is British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of stony, as in stony-broke, so more penniless.

clue.text: Back-number in the City? That's sickening

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the City's letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: back says the word for number is turned to read from right to left

parts.note: an item is a number on a programme or list

explanation.surface: A back issue found in London's financial district proves revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' makes METI and 'in' places it inside the postal district of the City, London's financial quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic substance induces vomiting, so it makes you sick.

clue.text: Beginning industrial action, so sure to get notice

definitions.meaning: so conspicuous that it is bound to be noticed

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is going on strike; the other is eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers downing tools are on strike, and something remarkable or conspicuous draws attention.

clue.text: Blot set out glass containers

indicators.note: out means the letters of blot set are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Ink smudges laid out on glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BLOT SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass vessels for wine or milk are flasks or jars.

clue.text: A good reason for being on the beach

parts.note: grounds are a good reason for something

explanation.surface: A good excuse for lounging on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the beach' means stranded on the shore, as a ship can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranded vessel is run onto the shore, out of the water.

clue.text: Players are thrown

explanation.definitionFit: A play's company of actors is its cast, and a ball cast is one that was hurled.

clue.text: Cross the top man and punishment ensues!

parts.note: to span is to cross, as a bridge does
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: Annoy the boss and a beating follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like annoy, but it means span.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking on the bottom is a chastisement.

clue.text: Destroying an insect for example

indicators.note: destroying means the letters of an insect are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Swatting a bug, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroying' rearranges AN INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A case or specimen illustrating something is a single occurrence.

clue.text: Account 26 correct

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: An account, cross-referenced, is spot on.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is CURATE, the junior minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and without error is precise.

clue.text: Keeping quiet over five hundred-27!

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Keeping silent on the subject of five hundred something.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is MERE, a lake, so the definition is a small body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small lake, much like a garden pool of still water.

clue.text: Increase the term of imprisonment

explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to pull it out, and a jail sentence is a spell inside in slang.

clue.text: A French man demands transport to school

parts.note: BR, British Rail, was Britain's state railway
Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A Frenchman insists on a lift to school.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the old national railway; Eton is an English boarding school. The answer is a native of Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Lie and upset a guy

indicators.note: upset means the letters of lie and are tipped over into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling a fib upsets a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges LIE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name stands for any fellow.

clue.text: Aperitif put by, show agreement

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
to nod is to signal yes

explanation.surface: Put the drink aside and nod in assent.
explanation.walkthrough: PER is Latin for by.
explanation.definitionFit: A French aniseed liqueur often taken before a meal.

clue.text: Not a rise negotiated for legal officials

indicators.note: negotiated means the letters of not a rise are worked into a new deal

explanation.surface: Lawyers' clerks find their pay claim refused after talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges NOT A RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: These lawyers witness signatures and certify documents.

clue.text: Junior minister!" a ne'er-do-well scoffed

parts.note: a cur is a worthless fellow
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: A layabout sneers at an underling in the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' here is a clergyman, not a politician: a junior priest assisting a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant clergyman in a parish ranks below the vicar or rector.

clue.text: Only a little time remains

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only a short time is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' points to the run hidden across 'time remains'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no more than it is called is just, simply.

clue.text: It's natural to find a hotel at one point

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
taken as written
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Finding a hotel at a given place is second nature.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) is one of the four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn qualities come naturally rather than being learned.

clue.text: Strange Oriental story

indicators.note: strange means the letters of oriental are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: A peculiar tale from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges ORIENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling or narration of events is a recounting, an account.

clue.text: Environmentally responsible English writer

parts.note: green means eco-friendly

explanation.surface: An eco-conscious English novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene was an English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene wrote novels such as Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Drove off, disgusted

explanation.definitionFit: Troops beat back an attacker, and something revolting leaves one sickened.
